narrativeBlocks.title: A debt of blood
narrativeBlocks.body: King Minos of Crete holds Athens under a terrible tribute: periodically, seven youths and seven maidens are shipped to Crete — food for the Minotaur, the man-bull monster sealed inside the labyrinth built by Daedalus.

narrativeBlocks.title: Theseus volunteers
narrativeBlocks.body: When the tribute falls due again, Theseus puts himself among the fourteen. His plan is not to escape it but to end it: he promises his father he will kill the Minotaur and sail home under a white sail.

narrativeBlocks.title: Ariadne's thread
narrativeBlocks.body: In Crete, Minos's daughter Ariadne falls in love with Theseus at first sight. Her gift is simple and decisive: a ball of thread. Tie one end at the entrance, unwind it through the maze, and the way back is never lost.

narrativeBlocks.title: The Minotaur
narrativeBlocks.body: Theseus winds his way into the heart of the labyrinth, finds the Minotaur, and kills it — in the plainest versions with his bare hands or a club. Then he follows the thread back out and leads the thirteen other captives to the ships.

narrativeBlocks.title: The labyrinth's afterlife
narrativeBlocks.body: The maze outlived the myth — 'labyrinth' became the word for any trap of your own design, and the story's machinery (love, a token, a monster in the dark) keeps being retold in modern fiction and games.
